title: Analytical method development and validation for the quantification of metaldehyde in soil
author: Keighley, Ramwell, et al.
materials: Methods in the literature [1] that detail metaldehyde extraction from soil tend to use methanol, or methanol/water solvents. This study based the extraction method on the published methods [1]. Initial method development to extract metaldehyde used a pasture clay loam soil, which was sampled from a livestock field in North Yorkshire and free from any known previous metaldehyde application. Soil samples (50 g dry weight basis) were weighed into 250 ml plastic screw-top containers, the moisture adjusted to 60% of maximum water holding capacity (MWHC) using deionized water and then left to settle for 30 min. The soil samples were spiked with metaldehyde (Sigma Aldrich, 99% purity) dissolved in water at three fortification levels (2.0, 0.2, and 0.02 mg kg soil−1) and left to equilibrate for 30 min. Extraction of metaldehyde comprised the addition of methanol (100 ml, analytical grade from Sigma Aldrich), shaking the containers at 200 rpm for 30 min on a side-to-side shaker, followed by centrifuging (Beckman Coulter, Allegra) for 5 min at 3500 rpm and decanting the supernatant into a centrifuge tube. This process was repeated in a second extraction using methanol (50 ml) and the second extract was stored separately. The samples were stored in a refrigerator at 4 °C prior to analysis by liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Three replicates were used as well as an untreated control.

Samples for LC-MS analysis were prepared by diluting 1/10 with water and filtered through a (Whatman) 0.2 μm pore nylon filter (Thermo Fischer Scientific). Calibration standards were matrix matched, produced from the same metaldehyde stock solution used for spiking the batch experiments, spiked into blank soil extract. The calibration range used included the following standards: 0.01 µg ml−1, 0.05 µg ml−1, 0.1 µg ml−1, 0.25 µg ml−1, 0.5 µg ml−1, 0.75 µg ml−1, 1.0 µg ml−1, and 2.5 µg ml−1. Calibration standards were produced by serial dilution of the 0.1 mg ml−1 metaldehyde (aq) stock solution used for the soil spiking. These were matrix-matched by amending the standards to 1/10 methanol used in a blank extraction of the test soil. A calibration curve is shown in Fig. 3.Fig. 3Calibration curve used for the method validation developed for the extraction of metaldehyde from soil.Fig 3

steps.title: Weigh and condition soil
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of dry soil into appropriate containers (250 ml screw‑top containers for the first development stage, 20 g into centrifuge tubes for the validation stage). Adjust the moisture to 60 % of the maximum water‑holding capacity (MWHC) using de‑ionised water and let the soil settle for 30 min.

steps.title: Spike soil with metaldehyde
steps.instruction: Prepare metaldehyde solutions (Sigma‑Aldrich, 99 % purity) in water and spike the soils to the required fortification levels:

substeps.instruction: First stage (50 g soil): 2.0 mg kg⁻¹, 0.2 mg kg⁻¹ and 0.02 mg kg⁻¹.
Second stage (20 g soil): 1.5 mg kg⁻¹ and 0.15 mg kg⁻¹ (additionally 0.015 mg kg⁻¹ for detection‑limit testing).

steps.title: Equilibrate spiked soils
steps.instruction: After spiking, mix thoroughly with a spatula and allow the soils to equilibrate for 30 min.

steps.title: First methanol extraction
steps.instruction: Add analytical‑grade methanol (Sigma‑Aldrich) to each sample, shake on a side‑to‑side shaker at 200 rpm for 30 min, then centrifuge at 3500 rpm for 5 min and decant the supernatant into a clean tube.

substeps.instruction: First development stage: add 100 ml methanol per 50 g soil.
Validation stage: add 25 ml methanol per 20 g soil.

steps.title: Second methanol extraction
steps.instruction: Repeat the extraction on the same soil residue with a second aliquot of methanol, shake, centrifuge and collect the supernatant separately (labelled Extract B).

substeps.instruction: First development stage: add 50 ml methanol.
Validation stage: add another 25 ml methanol.

steps.title: Store extracts
steps.instruction: Place all extracts (Extract A and Extract B) in a refrigerator at 4 °C until LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Dilute extracts and filter
steps.instruction: Dilute each extract 1 : 10 with de‑ionised water, then filter the diluted solution through a 0.2 µm nylon filter (Whatman, Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Prepare matrix‑matched calibration standards
steps.instruction: Using a metaldehyde stock solution of 0.1 mg ml⁻¹ (aq), prepare a series of calibration standards by serial dilution to obtain concentrations of 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 and 2.50 µg ml⁻¹. Matrix‑match each standard by adding the appropriate volume of blank soil extract (1 / 10 methanol from a blank extraction) so that the final solvent composition matches that of the samples.

steps.title: Prepare standard‑addition samples (optional)
steps.instruction: Make a metaldehyde stock solution of 0.01 mg ml⁻¹ in methanol. In 10 ml volumetric flasks add measured aliquots of this stock to 10 ml of supernatant obtained from the first extraction of a 0.01 mg kg⁻¹ fortified 50 g soil (extracted with 100 ml methanol). Prepare standards at 0.01, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.25 µg ml⁻¹ (not accounting for metaldehyde already present) and a supernatant‑only sample for a standard‑addition plot.

steps.title: Set up LC‑MS column and mobile phase
steps.instruction: Install the chosen column (final method uses a BEH phenyl 1.7 µm, 2.1 × 100 mm UPLC column; earlier trials used a Kinetex XB‑C18 2.6 µm, 50 × 2.1 mm column). Prepare mobile phase A: 1 mM ammonium acetate in ultrapure water; mobile phase B: methanol. Set the flow rate to 0.4 ml min⁻¹ (final method) or 0.5 ml min⁻¹ for the earlier SCIEX system.

steps.title: Configure MS detection parameters
steps.instruction: Set the mass spectrometer (SCIEX Qtrap 5500 or Waters Acquity‑Quattro Premier XE) to the following conditions:

substeps.instruction: Flow to the source: 0.5 ml min⁻¹ (SCIEX) or 0.4 ml min⁻¹ (Waters)
MRM transitions: m/z 106 (C₄H₈O₂ + NH₄⁺) and m/z 62 (C₂H₄O + NH₄⁺) with dwell time 160 ms
Acquisition window: 0.5–5.00 min (Waters method) with solvent delay 0.6 s

steps.title: Inject samples and acquire data
steps.instruction: Inject 1–5 µl of each filtered, diluted extract (and calibration/standard‑addition samples) into the LC‑MS system. Store injected vials at 4 °C prior to analysis if needed. Record peak areas for the two transitions and calculate metaldehyde concentrations using the matrix‑matched calibration curve (or standard‑addition plot).

description: Method validation results are presented in Table 3. The recovery of applied versus quantified metaldehyde was 100–132% for all soil types, 109% on average, with acceptably low relative standard deviation of < 20%. The proportion of metaldehyde present in the second sequential extraction (extract B) was higher for the more clayey, high organic content soil types, soil 2.4 and soil 6 S, illustrating the need for the second extraction step. These results demonstrated that applied metaldehyde could be extracted and quantified with a high recovery from different soil types.Table 3Method recoveries for the extraction of metaldehyde from different soil types (specifications in Table 1).
